Direct mechanical translation of research/studies/overnight-gap-behavior.md's (exp-032) Step 3 trigger: a significant gap-fill rate (~58% in both directions, 90% CIs entirely above 50%) and a significant negative correlation between gap size and the +90-minute forward return. This setup bets on the gap closing at the open -- direction=fade the gap, entry=today's 8:30 open, target=prior_close literally (not a risk-multiple like every other setup here), stop=symmetric 1:1 R:R, exit bounded at noon ET. 1340 raw signals (556 long, 784 short), 1061 resolved, 279 unresolved-by-noon-cutoff. Win rate 52.1% (CI 49.1%-55.1%) -- above 50%, consistent with the underlying gap-fill finding -- but the 1:1 R:R structure needs a materially higher win rate than that to overcome round-trip costs and the noon-cutoff exits' asymmetric average win (+0.92R) vs average loss (-1.17R). Expectancy -0.079R, 90% bootstrap CI -138.82R to -28.75R, entirely BELOW zero -- statistically decisive rejection, not a null result. Only 1.1% of forward-projected bootstrap sims ended net profitable. Important caveat carried over from exp-032 and stated up front in the setup doc: this rule was built from and first tested on the same Discovery slice that produced the underlying finding, so this is not an independent test either way -- but the result is decisively negative regardless, so the same-slice-circularity caveat doesn't need to be relitigated by a Validation-slice check here (there is no positive result to independently confirm). A real, previously-uncaught data edge case was found and fixed during this test: on Sundays, NQ's continuous-trading data only has bars from ~6pm ET onward (the weekly reopen), so a naive 'first bar at/after 8:30am' lookup was matching that evening reopen bar as if it were a real 8:30am entry -- crashed the backtest before being caught and fixed (370 such days excluded via a new entry_after_watch_window guard, now unit-tested). Verified separately that study_overnight_gap.py's own Step 1/2 results (exp-032) are NOT affected by this same issue -- both steps' time-windowed slices naturally come up empty for these degenerate days and get excluded via existing null-handling, not the fade-the-gap-specific guard. Full write-up: research/experiments/exp-033-fade-the-gap.md.

parameters.stop: entry +/- 1 sigma (fixed relative to entry, not a fixed band)

notes: First setup in this project sourced from external day-trading-technique research (Jason asked for a deep-research pass on widely-used techniques after Fade the Gap's rejection) rather than a market-structure concept applied fresh or a mechanical translation of this project's own characterization finding. Fades a close beyond the session VWAP's 2-sigma band back toward VWAP; stop at entry+/-1 sigma, target=VWAP, giving a 2:1-or-better R:R by construction. Largest sample and most decisive rejection of any setup tested in this project: 2081 raw signals (1009 long, 1072 short) on all but 20 of 2101 Discovery days -- the session's long open-ended watch window (up to ~15 hours) makes a 2-sigma excursion off session VWAP nearly a daily occurrence, not a rare event, an honest limitation flagged in the write-up. 2066 resolved, win rate 28.7% (CI 26.7%-30.6%), well short of the ~40%+ needed to be profitable at the realized ~1.93/1.65 average win/loss ratio. Expectancy -0.628R, 90% bootstrap CI -1450.38R to -1134.35R, entirely below zero -- the most decisive rejection and largest total-R loss (-1296.70R) of any setup tested here. TWO real implementation bugs were found and fixed during testing, both changing the frozen definition from its first draft: (1) the stop was originally a fixed VWAP+/-3-sigma band level, which landed on the wrong side of entry for ~17% of signals when a fast 1-minute move closed well past the 2-sigma trigger -- fixed by anchoring the stop to ENTRY (always exactly 1 sigma away) instead of a fixed band; (2) a small remaining fraction of signals had sigma small enough that entry and stop collapsed to the same value after 2-decimal rounding (a zero-risk signal, same failure class as detect_fvg_entry.py's earlier zero-risk-signal fix) -- fixed by skipping and continuing to watch rather than returning a degenerate signal. Both fixes are unit-tested regressions. Full write-up: research/experiments/exp-034-vwap-mean-reversion.md.

notes: exp-048: Jason's own risk-management idea (defined stop-loss, hold until doubling winnings), applied to exp-047's weekly trend signal via a hard -1R stop / +2R take-profit cap, sized off a 20-day ATR, checked against real intraday price path. Advisor-reviewed twice (v1->v2 for six required changes including disclosed selection risk and a pre-registered pilot tabulation; a second consultation chose a hard cap over a trailing exit to avoid a cross-week position-state architecture change). Jason signed off by delegating the final design choice to the Advisor. Result: mean +10.53 pts/week, 90% CI [-6.37, +28.38], spans zero -- not statistically credible. Roughly HALF the mean and a WIDER CI than exp-047's own near-miss (mean +19.38, CI [-1.165, +40.414]). Advisor-confirmed as the expected signature of a hard take-profit cap removing the small number of large trending weeks that drive this signal's edge -- a structural mismatch between the overlay and the signal's own source of edge, not a parameter-tuning issue. Line of inquiry closed per the frozen spec's pre-commitment; no retuning of the ATR window or R:R ratio on this data. Rejects this specific capped design, not the underlying risk-management idea in general -- a trailing-exit variant would need its own fresh, independently pre-registered hypothesis. notes: exp-049: second follow-on attempt on exp-047's near-miss, per the Advisor's own suggested next step (trailing exit instead of hard cap). Result: mean +10.20 pts/week, 90% CI [-6.88, +27.87], spans zero -- nearly identical to exp-048's hard-cap result (mean +10.53, CI [-6.37, +28.38]), contrary to the expectation that trailing would preserve more of the raw signal's tail. Diagnostic on exit R-multiples (run on already-generated data) showed 91.9% of stop/trail exits were the plain -1R stop, trail never activating -- only 12/299 weeks ever reached the +2R activation level, confirming no implementation bug, just that a 1R trail is too tight relative to NQ's weekly volatility to meaningfully extend past a hard cap. Per the frozen spec's pre-commitment, this is the second follow-on attempt without a clear pass -- the exp-047 weekly trend-following signal family (raw + all overlay variants) is now SHELVED. A wider trail distance is a real next idea but explicitly not pursued here, to avoid a post-hoc parameter search; would need its own fresh, independently pre-registered hypothesis. exp-051, frozen spec research/studies/cross-asset-weekly-trend-scoping.md (v2). 300 portfolio-weeks (2015-2021-10-03 Discovery slice). Primary: mean weekly net portfolio return (inverse-vol-weighted, 4 instruments, return-space) = 0.0002993, 90% CI (-0.0002691, 0.0008933) -- crosses zero, fails statistical-credibility gate (check 1). Economic-meaningfulness gate (check 2) cleared. Per the frozen spec's Section 3 lineage disclosure, this is the 4th test on the exp-047 signal family -- a pass would have earned eligibility for further corroboration, not promotion; a REJECTED verdict here per the pre-registered Section 11 follow-up plan means kill, not followed by parameter variants on this construction. Per-instrument means: NQ +0.001611, ZN +0.000223, 6E +0.000115, CL -0.001140 (CL's own result not economically meaningful) -- result not concentrated in one instrument, all but CL positive, consistent direction. NOTE: a real bug was found and fixed before this final run -- WTI crude legitimately traded negative on 2020-04-20/21 (the well-known May-2020 contract expiry event), which broke the log-return math (log of a non-positive price is undefined) and silently produced NaN through the whole pipeline on the first run. Fixed in study_volatility_regime.py's compute_daily_ref_closes() by treating a non-positive reference close as 'no usable close', the same general validity precondition already applied to a day with no bars at all -- not a parameter chosen after seeing a result, and a no-op for every other instrument/study on record (verified none of NQ/ZN/6E/ES ever had a non-positive close).

parameters.split_variable: causal expanding-tercile volatility regime (classify_regimes, reused unmodified)

notes: exp-053 (EXPLORATORY, re-mines exp-047/hyp-000017 Discovery data -- deliberate, disclosed one-time exception to that hypothesis notes stated no-re-mine commitment, per Jason request 2026-09-07 and Advisor guidance). Split exp-047 NQ weekly trend momentum (299 weeks) into 3 pre-existing causal volatility regimes (low/mid/high, reused classify_regimes() unmodified, no new lookahead). LOW-vol regime (n=111) clears the bar cleanly: mean +24.32 pts/week, 90pct CI [3.66, 44.46], statistically credible AND economically meaningful. MID (n=65) and HIGH (n=123) regimes do not clear (MID: mean -14.18, CI spans zero; HIGH: mean +32.65, CI spans zero despite large magnitude). Advisor-reviewed same day: result should be substantially discounted (post-hoc 3-way split of already-marginal near-miss data, CI not adjusted for the split search, true lower bound likely closer to zero than +3.66 states); low-vol regime also has only 7 position flips in 111 weeks, suggesting few independent long stable stretches rather than 111 truly independent observations -- effective sample size may be much smaller than n=111 implies. Boring explanations not yet ruled out: fewer whipsaws/lower cost drag in calm weeks, and whether the 111 weeks cluster into just a handful of contiguous calendar stretches. STATUS: hypothesis-generating only, NOT evidence, NOT promoted. Required next step per exp-047 own pre-commitment and Advisor: pre-register "trend-following in low-vol weeks specifically" as its own hypothesis and test it on data never touched by any test of this signal family (Validation/Holdout), not on this Discovery slice again. Full detail: src/study_nq_trend_volatility_regime_split.py.

parameters.filter: low-volatility-regime weeks only (classify_regimes, unchanged, from exp-053/hyp-000023)

notes: exp-054: pre-registered prospective test of exp-053/hyp-000023 exploratory lead (NQ 52-week trend momentum restricted to low-volatility-regime weeks) on the Validation slice (2021-10-04 to 2024-01-03), genuinely new data for this signal family. Signal/filter unchanged from exp-047/exp-053, warm-up computed continuously across Discovery+Validation (no cold restart at the boundary), only Validation-window weeks scored. RESULT: INCONCLUSIVE, not a clean statistical disproof -- only 8 weeks in the entire ~117-week Validation slice were classified low-volatility by the causal expanding-tercile classifier (dominated by the much larger Discovery-period pool), too few to compute a meaningful confidence interval. Background/context: the unfiltered signal on the same Validation slice also barely moved (only 2 position flips in 117 weeks) and its own CI spans zero. Honest reading: this Validation window may simply not have contained many weeks the classifier would call calm relative to the full multi-year history -- the test was underpowered, not a rejection of the hypothesis with evidence against it. Per the pre-registered decision rule (no retuning of the threshold/window on this result) and the exp-047 no-re-mine discipline, this specific line (low-vol regime filter on the raw 52-week NQ momentum signal) is closed for now -- logged REJECTED as this project logs any non-clearing result, but future-reader should not read this as strong evidence the effect is false, only that this test could not confirm it. A meaningful re-test would need either a longer Validation-equivalent window or a regime classifier re-baselined per-period -- neither pursued here, per pre-commitment. Full detail: src/study_nq_trend_low_vol_prospective_validation.py.

exp-055: pilot of the collective-evidence research methodology Jason proposed 2026-09-07, scoped narrow to the trend familys own 4 correlated variants (exp-047/048/049/051), per his own decision after a mechanical near-miss ranking showed no bench of independent near-misses exists outside this family yet. Frozen spec: research/studies/collective-evidence-pilot-scoping.md, Advisor-reviewed (required addition incorporated: 11-bucket multiple-comparisons accounting, 30-distinct-week eligibility floor). DISCLOSED SCOPE LIMIT: this is a dry run of the aggregation machinery (week-level dedup, outcome-vs-baseline scoring), not a test of independent cross-strategy corroboration -- the 4 lenses share one underlying signal. RESULT across 4 pre-registered conditions (11 buckets, all met the 30-week eligibility floor): 10 of 11 buckets show a 90pct CI spanning 0.5 (no real deviation from baseline). ONE bucket stands out: distance_from_52wk_ma = low (weeks where price sits close to its own 52-week average, i.e. a weak-trend reading), n=42 distinct weeks, mean fraction of lenses beating their own baseline = 0.268, 90pct CI (0.185, 0.357) -- entirely BELOW 0.5, meaning these trend-following lenses collectively underperform their own typical week specifically when the market is not trending far from its average. This is directionally sensible (trend signals should struggle when there is little trend) rather than a surprising fluke, but per the pre-registered next-step rule it is a candidate only, not a finding -- requires its own single pre-registered prospective test on the Validation slice (the exp-053->054 pattern) before being trusted. Machinery itself worked cleanly: all 11 buckets computed, eligibility floor correctly gated every bucket, no bucket was reported as a false candidate. Full detail: src/study_collective_evidence_pilot.py, data/study_collective_evidence_pilot_results.json.
